promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Concept and uses of classification systems

questions.q: Which mnemonic is commonly used to summarise the seven characteristics of living organisms?
questions.explain: MRS GREN stands for movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion and nutrition.

questions.q: How is respiration defined as a characteristic of living organisms?
options: The chemical reactions in cells that break down nutrient molecules and release energy for metabolism
The removal of waste products of metabolism from the body
The taking in of gases through the surface of the body
The movement of oxygen into and carbon dioxide out of the lungs
questions.explain: Respiration releases energy from nutrient molecules for use in metabolic processes within cells.

questions.q: Which life process is the removal from organisms of the waste products of metabolism, toxic materials and substances in excess of requirements?
questions.explain: Excretion removes metabolic wastes such as carbon dioxide and urea, unlike egestion which removes undigested food.

questions.q: Which statement best defines growth in living organisms?
options: A permanent increase in size and dry mass by an increase in cell number, cell size, or both
A temporary swelling caused by the absorption of water
The production of new organisms of the same kind
The change in position of part of an organism
questions.explain: Growth is a permanent increase in size and dry mass, distinguishing it from temporary changes such as water uptake.

questions.q: A plant shoot growing towards a source of light is an example of which characteristic of living organisms?
questions.explain: Detecting and responding to a change such as the direction of light is sensitivity.

questions.q: How is a species defined?
options: A group of organisms that can reproduce to produce fertile offspring
A group of organisms that live in the same habitat
A group of organisms with the same number of chromosomes
A group of organisms that look identical to one another
questions.explain: Members of a species can interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

questions.q: In the binomial system of naming, the two parts of a scientific name refer to which categories?
questions.explain: The binomial system gives each organism a two-part name showing its genus followed by its species.

questions.q: In the binomial name Panthera leo, which part indicates the genus?
questions.explain: The first name, Panthera, is the genus and the second name, leo, is the species.

questions.q: Which is the correct way to write the scientific name of the human species?
questions.explain: The genus begins with a capital letter and the species with a lower-case letter, both written in italics.

questions.q: Modern classification groups organisms mainly using evidence from which source?
options: The sequences of bases in DNA
The size and colour of the organism
The habitat in which it lives
The geographical region where it is found
questions.explain: Studying DNA base sequences reveals evolutionary relationships more reliably than external appearance alone.

questions.q: The base sequence of a gene in species W is compared with the same gene in three other species. Which species is most closely related to W?
options: The species with the most similar base sequence to W
The species with the most different base sequence to W
The species that lives closest to W
The species that is the same size as W
questions.explain: Organisms sharing a more recent common ancestor have more similar base sequences.

questions.q: Which set correctly lists the five kingdoms used in classification?
questions.explain: The five kingdoms are animals, plants, fungi, prokaryotes and protoctists; viruses are not placed in a kingdom.

questions.q: An organism has cell walls not made of cellulose, no chloroplasts, and feeds by saprotrophic nutrition. To which kingdom does it belong?
questions.explain: Fungi have cell walls made of chitin, lack chloroplasts and feed saprotrophically or parasitically.

questions.q: Which pair of features distinguishes cells of the plant kingdom from those of the animal kingdom?
options: Cell walls made of cellulose and the presence of chloroplasts
Cell walls made of chitin and the absence of a nucleus
The presence of flagella and stored glycogen
The absence of a cell membrane and presence of plasmids
questions.explain: Plant cells have cellulose cell walls and chloroplasts for photosynthesis, which animal cells lack.

questions.q: Which feature is characteristic of a prokaryote such as a bacterium?
options: A cell wall made of cellulose
questions.explain: Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus; their circular DNA lies free in the cytoplasm.

questions.q: An arthropod has three pairs of legs, a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen, and one pair of antennae. To which group does it belong?
questions.explain: Insects have three pairs of legs, three body sections and a single pair of antennae.

questions.q: An arthropod has four pairs of legs, a body in two sections and no antennae. To which group does it belong?
questions.explain: Arachnids, such as spiders, have four pairs of legs, two body sections and no antennae.

questions.q: Which group of vertebrates has wet scales, fins, breathes using gills and reproduces by external fertilisation?
questions.explain: Fish are covered in wet scales, use fins and gills, and typically fertilise their eggs externally in water.

questions.q: How does a dichotomous key identify an unknown organism?
options: Through a series of steps that each offer two contrasting choices
By measuring the total mass of the organism
By comparing the number of chromosomes
By recording the temperature of the organism
questions.explain: A dichotomous key uses paired statements at each step, each pointing to the next step or a name.

questions.q: Use this key: 1 Wings present, go to 2 / Wings absent = Spider. 2 One pair of wings = Housefly / Two pairs of wings = Butterfly. An organism with two pairs of wings is identified as which?
questions.explain: Wings present leads to step 2, and two pairs of wings leads to the identification of Butterfly.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) syllabus; Characteristics & Classification
